- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model underestimates upside; add 2–4% buffer to forecast.
- Model frequently underestimates long-term (30d) mean reversion after strong upward moves; adjust downward by 1–3% if sentiment turns neutral or mildly negative.
- When sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model overestimates upside; reduce forecast by 3–5%.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 5–7 days of forecast) — especially if sentiment is volatile — add 1–2% to forecast to account for momentum.
- If sentiment is negative and price is trending upward, model often fails to recognize sentiment-driven reversal; reduce forecast by 2–5% in 10–15 day horizon.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if sentiment is negative and price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect mean reversion bias.
